content.content: When `record --from <handle> --to <node>` is invoked with an open draft, the deccy CLI shall record the changed paths of the landable set — the target change's current owned set together with the ref paths the draft's node document adds — into that node's change and shall turn that draft's record `landed` inside the same recording.
content.rationale:
Every element of the requirement states an answer a prerequisite has already given, so the sentence fixes which side of each answer is required rather than reopening it (uvrltuvo, rvyrosmp, qvkuluyw, vkkwusty).

The trigger names the source form of `record`, not a verb of its own, and names the draft it reads as an open one. uvrltuvo settles both: `record --from <handle> --to <node> [path...]` is the recording the verb already is, reached through a different selection of the edits, `--to` stays required in both forms and still names the one change the edits enter, and only an open draft lands. vkkwusty supplies the states whose `open` side is that precondition. Nothing in the trigger chooses how a handle is minted or a draft opened; uvrltuvo leaves both to the records that own them, and the requirement takes the handle as the source arrives.

The recorded-path clause is uvrltuvo's landable set stated as what a landing must record, and that set has two sources neither of which narrows the other. The first is the target change's current owned set: its node document plus the repo-relative paths its `content.ref` lists when that field is an array, and the node document alone when it is inline. The second is the draft's node document, read from the draft's own workspace; writing that document into the target's change makes owned every ref path it newly lists, so those edits are changed paths of the same union. The changed paths a landing records are the changed paths of that union and nothing else — not the draft workspace's other files, not the target change's other files, and not a dirty set read as ownership — and every changed path of the union is placed by the one recording the landing is, because the draft has no second landing in which a leftover could be placed. Taking the set from one source alone is the defect the union fixes: from the current owned set alone, a ref path the draft's node document adds is changed content the recording itself makes owned and does not place, and from the draft's document alone, a ref path the draft drops is excluded even though the target change still owns it and the draft may carry a deletion to place. rvyrosmp supplies what the recording itself is: it places the named edits into the named node's change, creates no node and no change, draws no edge, and lands nothing outside an owning change. That is why the requirement says "into that node's change" and stops there; the destination is the one change `--to` names, which uvrltuvo has already agreed with the node the draft names, and the encoding of the comparison that finds the changed paths of the union is left where uvrltuvo leaves it.

The landed clause is vkkwusty's transition stated as the second half of the same act. A record has exactly two states, `open` and `landed`, the only transition is `open` → `landed`, it happens when the draft lands, and a landed record is retained; the requirement therefore turns that draft's record `landed` and says nothing about a third state, a reopening, a second landing or a deletion. qvkuluyw fixes where that write sits: for every landing the recording marks the draft's record `landed` and retains it, and that update is partial work inside the recording — not a second operation, not a fourth member of the operation vocabulary, and not separately bracketed. "Inside the same recording" is that placement read back as a requirement, and it is why the two clauses of the requirement are joined by "and" as one recording rather than stated as two acts — the union placed by the recording, and the draft's record turned `landed` inside that same recording rather than beside it.

No element contradicts a parent, and no element adds a commitment none of the four fixes. The sentence does not say how a handle is generated or a draft opened, how a source resolves to a jj change, how the `--to` agreement or the source-that-is-the-target refusal is tested, how staleness is compared or which paths a stale refusal names, the wording, order, stream or exit status of any refusal, the order in which refusals are tested, what the source form's optional path arguments do when given, or how the recording is undone. Each of those is either decided in a prerequisite and taken here as stated (uvrltuvo, vkkwusty) or placed outside them (uvrltuvo, qvkuluyw), so restating or narrowing one here would make the requirement the owner of a choice it does not need to hold; the requirement fixes only the one landing the source form performs — the changed paths of the union into the change `--to` names, and the draft's record turned `landed` inside that same recording.
